summary: Haaretz reported that Ben-Gvir used an Israel Police helicopter to travel from a private northern vacation to public events in central Israel and back toward his vacation; the same police-volunteer event had been permitted only after his sworn commitment not to campaign there.
notes: No formal post-event Elections Committee finding establishing a campaign breach and no sufficiently complete official helicopter authorization/response record were recovered. A separate CEC decision allowed the police event subject to the no-campaign undertaking; that does not adjudicate helicopter-resource use. Preserve Pending; do not infer illegality or motive.

summary: During/after Ben-Gvir's filmed visit to Palestinian women prisoners at Damon Prison, the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel asked the Central Elections Committee chair to order the video removed and to bar further publicized prison visits through the election period.
notes: The exact Damon video is independently documented and Ben-Gvir's own statements are recoverable, but searches through Sept. 2 still did not surface an Elections Committee ruling on this specific petition. Keep Pending; do not label the visit illegal or an established campaign breach absent a ruling or stronger official finding.

summary: Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg issued a temporary injunction ordering Netanyahu to remove a campaign video showing him interacting and taking selfies with children at Jerusalem's Malha Mall.
notes: Primary petition/order bundle identifies TBC 114/26 and the exact original Aug. 11 verified Facebook video. The injunction is expressly temporary and further proceedings were contemplated. Fresh searches through Sept. 2 found no final ruling; preserve Pending and do not convert the interim order into a final adjudication.

summary: Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg issued a temporary injunction ordering Religious Zionism to remove an AI-generated campaign video featuring young children discussing Smotrich's reserve-duty plan until a petition over use of children under 15 in campaign material could be adjudicated.
notes: Exact original Smotrich X status 2090119271485444585 remains preserved. Fresh searches through Sept. 2 did not recover a final ruling. Preserve the interim status; do not convert it into a final violation finding.

summary: Central Elections Committee chair Justice Noam Sohlberg partially accepted a petition over Ben-Gvir's 46-second Jaffa campaign video, found it to be election propaganda, and ordered edits: remove segments featuring police without Ben-Gvir or officers outside his security detail, and blur identifiable uniformed police from his security detail where possible.
notes: Newly surfaced candidate. Ynet, News1, Makor Rishon and Arutz 7 independently report the same Aug. 9 ruling and limiting outcome; News1 preserves the material defense and exculpatory details: most requested relief was denied, Sohlberg did not impose a blanket ban on professional tours/secured appearances, and no costs were ordered. The exact May 6 message ('הגעתי ליפו... יש פה בעל בית') is independently archived, but this run did not recover the primary CEC decision document or a stable exact original video URL. Keep Pending rather than accept from secondary reporting alone; prioritize primary-decision and original-media recovery next run.
